title: On the Universality of Deep Contextual Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Literature review of performance disparities between high-resource and low-resource languages on massively multilingual benchmarks like XTREME.
Surveying existing empirical studies on model performance degradation when processing non-standard regional dialects (e.g., Singaporean English) and localized language variations.

Reviewing prior research that demonstrates performance disparities based on author age, gender, and ethnicity, such as differential POS tagging accuracy on texts by older authors and gender stereotypes in embeddings.
Synthesizing research on the sub-optimal performance of standard language models when evaluating informal text formats, such as social media posts and texting, compared to formal written text.
Evaluating literature on diachronic semantic change and the limitations of language models in accurately processing word senses across different historical time periods.
